title: The Snipe Pleads
text:
Once there was a hunter who was out in the forest, and there he met a little snipe.

“Dear friend, don’t shoot my children!” said the snipe.

“And what kind are your children, then?” the hunter asked.
imagePrompt: In a quiet forest clearing, The Hunter—a practical woodsman in simple outdoor clothes—pauses mid-step as The Snipe, a small speckled bird and proud mother, flutters close in front of him with wings spread in a desperate plea, her bright eyes fixed on him as if begging for mercy.

title: A Grim Return
text:
“The prettiest children that walk in the whole forest are mine!” the snipe answered.

“Then I suppose I mustn’t shoot them,” said the hunter.

But when he came back, he had in his hand a whole bunch of young snipe he had shot.
imagePrompt: Along a mossy woodland path, The Hunter strides back holding a dangling bunch of The Young Snipes by their thin legs—ordinary-looking, small, brown-speckled chicks—while The Snipe hovers nearby in shock and disbelief, her feathers ruffled against the still green of the forest.

title: Ugliest Ones
text:
“Oh, oh! Why did you shoot my children anyway?” cried the snipe.

“Were these yours?” the hunter asked. “I only shot the ugliest ones I could find.”

“Oh yes,” said the snipe. “Don’t you know that everyone thinks their own children are the best?”
imagePrompt: Under the shade of low branches, The Hunter lifts one of The Young Snipes in his hand as if asking a blunt question, his face calm and matter-of-fact, while The Snipe perches close by, distressed yet stubbornly protective, her posture tense as she confronts the painful misunderstanding about which chicks were “prettiest.”
